questions.q: Why do you pass a seed to np.random.default_rng(2024)?
options: It makes the numbers truly random instead of pseudo-random
It makes the simulation run faster
It makes the same sequence of numbers come out every run, so results are reproducible
It guarantees the sample matches the theoretical distribution exactly
questions.explain: A seed fixes the starting state of the pseudo-random generator so the results can be repeated by you and by others.

questions.q: rng.integers(1, 7, size=5) is used to simulate five rolls of a die. Why is the upper bound 7?
options: The upper bound of integers() is excluded, so 7 gives values 1 through 6
A die has seven faces
The lower bound is excluded
numpy adds one to every argument
questions.explain: integers(low, high) draws from low up to but not including high by default.

questions.q: What is a Monte Carlo simulation?
options: A formula that gives exact probabilities
A way to estimate a quantity by repeating a random experiment many times and summarizing the results
A test that proves data is normally distributed
A method that removes outliers from a dataset
questions.explain: Monte Carlo methods approximate answers, such as probabilities or percentiles, by simulating many random trials.

questions.q: Your simulation of daily revenue assumes each of the 50 orders is returned independently at 30%. If in reality a bad batch causes many returns together, what is the likely effect?
options: The simulation overstates the risk
The simulation is unaffected
The simulation understates the risk of very bad days
The simulation would give an error
questions.explain: Clustered returns create more extreme days than independent returns do, so an independence assumption makes the tail look thinner than it really is.

questions.q: You increase a simulation from 10,000 to 40,000 draws. Roughly how does the random error change?
options: It drops to about half
It drops to a quarter
It stays the same
It doubles
questions.explain: Monte Carlo error shrinks roughly with the square root of the number of draws, so 4 times the draws gives about half the error.
